source: data/decks.json (placed lists), data/synergy.json, the catalog, docs/archetypes.md, docs/research.md
note: Questions, not findings: a long-legal card that fits a legend's engine by its text, that the legend's winning lists skip and some other legend plays heavily. The evidence is counted; the hypotheses are the usual explanations, checked against the numbers; the answer is hand-written in docs/research.md.

verdicts.skip: Winners are right to skip it

Rek'Sai, Void Burrower.doc: reveal — the top of the deck. Conquer, flip two, play one: the legend on conquest,

Irelia, Blade Dancer.doc: ready → move → draw (Herder). Her idea page's Engines panel lists the Radiance

Kha'Zix, Voidreaver.doc: movement — Faefolk, Void Assault, Ride the Wind, Tideturner, the legend's walk-home.

items.title: Why do Kennen, Heart of the Tempest's winners skip Evelynn, Entrancing?
evidence: 75 placed lists. Plays from elsewhere > Movement > Trash size > Facedown, strongest first.
hypotheses: Facedown is this deck's #4 engine; its main one is Plays from elsewhere. Its cards here may be insurance, not a plan.
A payoff is worth what it multiplies: here 2 Tornado Warrior, 2 Switcheroo, 1 Tideturner.
The winning list averages 2.8 Energy with 22 of 40 cards at 2 or less; the most-asked Power is Chaos 20, Order 1.
New cards add 5 to Facedown in these colours (Momentary Companion, The Waters' Wage, Demon Shade, Gutter Guardian, …); an old reason may not hold.

why: competes at 2 Energy with Traveling Merchant, Shadow Order Disciple, Tideturner

cards.answer: As the engine answer, and smaller still: Karthus doubles what Rek'Sai's Deathknells give — a 1-Might Bird, an exhausted Gold, two Recruits once Empowered — for 3 Energy and the deck's scarcest Power (Order). It is a 3-Might body that does nothing on the turn it is played, in a deck that wins by having more bodies at more battlefields than the opponent can answer. Doubling Ruined Rex (LeBlanc) is a different card. The discovery report's first lead was this card, and it was wrong. Whether it stacks with Detonation Amplifier is also unsettled by the rules (only Repeat stacks, §820.3) — a second reason not to build around it.

items.answer: Rek'Sai's engine is the top of the deck, not deaths: conquer, reveal two, play one, with Breacher's Accelerate and Undertitan's [Add] 2 paying off what arrives that way. The deck is cheap bodies so that almost anything it flips is playable (27 of 40 cards at 2 Energy or less), and its Deathknell units are insurance that makes a lost fight cheap (guides/reksai-void-burrower.md §6). The payoffs add little when flipped or when they fight: the 3-Energy ones (Karthus, Black Rose Dignitary, Loyal Poro) would take the slot of Faithful Manufactor and Breacher, the 2-Energy ones (Soaring Scout, Unsung Hero) that of Inferna and the Deathknell bodies they would pay off, and the Order payoffs compete for the Order Power that Undertitan, Vanguard Captain and Cull the Weak already ask for. LeBlanc plays these cards because LeBlanc's deck is the Deathknell deck; Rek'Sai's winners, 0 of 61, are right not to.
